title: For every partition lambda and signed bicomposition of n, the row-admissible permutations of Theorem 3.3 define the explicit integral homomorphisms from the Specht lattice to the signed Young permutation lattice
author: Kay Jin Lim; Kai Meng Tan
source_title: Homomorphisms from Specht Modules to Signed Young Permutation Modules
difficulty_reason: The unsigned Young-permutation construction does not directly survive when column colors carry signs. The author isolates exactly the stabilizer condition needed for well-defined coefficients and proves descent through the integral Specht relations. An explicit involution cancels all Garnir contributions, giving a uniform integral construction rather than an appeal to semisimple character multiplicities.
source_version: Official SIGMA 14 (2018) article 038, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2018.038; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

proof_review.note: The complete new signed homomorphism construction3.3 and all essential local proofs3.5-3.16 were read. The author establishes the precise row-intersection condition R for a well-defined sign projection, proves coefficient transformation and cancellation identities, and shows the tableau map is equivariant and kills column and Garnir relations. The Garnir cancellation uses an explicit fixed-point-free sign-reversing involution. The integral Specht presentation is justified by standard-tableau straightening and freeness, permitting descent over Z and subsequent scalar extension to any field. No semisimple spanning/basis theorem or characteristic-dependent independence neighbor is separately counted.

statement_scope: Full Theorem3.3 over Z for a partition lambda of n and a bicomposition (alpha,beta) of n, a fixed reference tableau t0 and any left transversal Gamma of S_(alpha,beta). For every d in R={d: d^-1*R_t0*d intersect S_(alpha,beta) is contained in S_alpha}, the exact author signed coefficient sum defines a Z*S_n-module homomorphism S_Z^lambda to M_Z(alpha,beta). Preserve the epsilon_d projection and all indexing conventions. These maps may vanish; no universal nonvanishing, basis or spanning assertion in positive characteristic is added.
